title: The four operations and the inverse

board_content.text: Multiply like two binomials, replace $i^2$ with $-1$, then collect.
For division, multiply top and bottom by $c-id$ so the denominator becomes the real number $c^2+d^2$.
Leaving a complex denominator is not standard form.

segments_english.text: Let's gather the four operations in one place — this is the machinery every later subtopic assumes is automatic.
Addition is easy: add the real parts and add the imaginary parts. z one plus z two is a plus c, all plus i times b plus d.
Subtraction is the same idea with minus signs: a minus c, plus i times b minus d.
Multiplication is where i earns its keep. z one times z two equals a c minus b d, plus i times a d plus b c.
You don't memorize that as a formula; you just multiply the two brackets like ordinary binomials, replace i squared by minus one wherever it appears, and collect real and imaginary parts.
Division is the interesting one. z one over z two equals a c plus b d, plus i times b c minus a d, all over c squared plus d squared.
The trick behind it: multiply top and bottom by c minus i d. That turns the denominator into the real number c squared plus d squared, and now you can split into real and imaginary parts cleanly.
The multiplicative inverse is just one over z: it equals a minus i b over a squared plus b squared, valid whenever z is not zero.
And a standing rule for the whole chapter: never leave a complex number sitting in a denominator. An answer with a complex denominator is not in standard form.

segments_hinglish.text: Chaaron operations ek jagah rakhte hain — ye wo machinery hai jo har baad wale subtopic automatic maanta hai.
Addition aasan hai: real parts add karo aur imaginary parts add karo. z one plus z two hai a plus c, poora plus i times b plus d.
Subtraction wahi idea minus signs ke saath: a minus c, plus i times b minus d.
Multiplication mein i apni keemat vasool karta hai. z one times z two barabar a c minus b d, plus i times a d plus b c.

Isko formula ki tarah rattne ki zaroorat nahi; bas dono brackets ko ordinary binomials ki tarah multiply karo, jahan i square dikhe use minus one se replace karo, aur real aur imaginary parts collect karo.
Division interesting hai. z one over z two barabar a c plus b d, plus i times b c minus a d, poora over c square plus d square.
Iske peeche trick: top aur bottom ko c minus i d se multiply karo. Isse denominator ban jaata hai real number c square plus d square, aur ab aap real aur imaginary parts cleanly alag kar sakte ho.
Multiplicative inverse bas one over z hai: barabar a minus i b over a square plus b square, valid jab bhi z zero na ho.
Aur poore chapter ke liye ek pakka rule: complex number ko kabhi denominator mein mat chhodo. Complex denominator wala answer standard form mein nahi hai.
